title.narrative: Response to the Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals and Host Community (EA/2025)

description.narrative:
There are currently 1.3 million Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh living in temporary settlements spread across 33 congested camps in Cox’s Bazar District, Bangladesh. In 2024, escalating violence created a new large influx of Rohingya civilians to the camps, increasing pressure on the services in the camps. The refugees lack formal legal status, face extreme restrictions on movement and are not permitted to legally work. The existing response capacity has been overwhelmed by new arrivals, whilst at the same time suffering from ever-decreasing funding committed by the international community. There is immense strain on infrastructure, services, resources and the local environment. The Government of Bangladesh and local communities have supported the refugees to the best of their ability, but tensions are rising as the number of refugees increases, funding reduces, and global attention focuses on new conflicts and crises.
Caritas Bangladesh (CB) was one of the first humanitarian actors to respond in 2017. It has been continuously responding to the emergency needs of Rohingya refugees since then despite the intense pressure on funds: the EA/2024 was only 50% funded. They have provided shelter, food, Non-Food Items, site improvements, WASH, education, livelihoods support, and have implemented disaster risk reduction initiatives. CB has also supported community-based protection which has become an urgent focus over the past 2 years. Reductions in funding support, a lack of livelihood options, human trafficking and continuing violence in Myanmar have resulted in growing frustration and hopelessness. This has led to even higher levels of insecurity and violence in the camps which affects both refugees and humanitarian staff.
Between 2017 and 2024, Caritas Bangladesh reached 1,353,272 million people. This contribution will go towards CB's 2025 emergency appeal which will support 117,610 people in Cox's Bazar.
